questions.q: The term independent of $x$ in the expansion of \left(\frac{(x+1)}{\left(x^{2 / 3}+1-x^{1 / 3}\right)}-\frac{(x+1)}{\left(x-x^{1 / 2}\right)}\right)^{10}, x\gt1$ is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \left(\frac{(x+1)}{\left(x^{\frac{2}{3}}+1-x^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)}-\frac{(x-1)}{\left(x-x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)}\right)^{10} \\ & =\left(\left(x^{\frac{1}{3}}+1\right)-\left(\frac{\sqrt{x}+1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)\right)^{10} \\ & =\left(x^{\frac{1}{3}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)^{10} \\ & T_{r+1}={ }^{10} C_r(x)^{\frac{10-r}{3}}(-1)^r(x)^{-\frac{r}{2}} \\ & \frac{10-r}{3}-\frac{r}{2}=0 \\ & (20-2 r)-3 r=0 \\ & r^{10}=4 \\ & \Rightarrow{ }^{10} C_4(-1)^4=210\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The number of ordered pairs  \left(r, k\right)$ for which $6 . {C}_{r} 35 = \left(k^{2} - 3\right) . {C}_{r + 1} 36 ,$ where $k$ is an integer& is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $6 . {C}_{r} 35 = \left(k^{2} - 3\right) . {C}_{r + 1} 36$

$⇒ \dfrac{36}{r + 1}{×}^{35}{C}_{r}\left(k^{2} - 3\right) = 6{×}^{35}{C}_{r}$, using properties of binomial coefficient.
$⇒ k^{2} - 3 = \dfrac{r + 1}{6}$

$⇒ k^{2} = 3 + \dfrac{r + 1}{6}$

$r$ can be $5,35$

For $r = 5, k = \pm 2$

$r = 35, k = \pm 3$

Hence, number of solution~$= 4$

questions.q:
If $b$ is very small as compared to the value of $a$, so that the cube and other higher powers of $\dfrac{b}{a}$ can be neglected in the identity

$\dfrac{1}{a - b} + \dfrac{1}{a - 2b} + \dfrac{1}{a - 3b} + \ldots . + \dfrac{1}{a - nb} = \alphan + \betan^{2} + \gamman^{3}$

then the value of $\gamma$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{1}{a - b} + \dfrac{1}{a - 2b} + \dfrac{1}{a - 3b} + \ldots . + \dfrac{1}{a - nb}$

$= \left(a - b\right)- 1 + \left(a - 2b\right)- 1 + \ldots . + \left(a - nb\right)- 1$

$= \dfrac{1}{a}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\left(1 - \dfrac{rb}{a}\right)- 1$

$= \dfrac{1}{a}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\left\{\left(1 + \dfrac{rb}{a} + \dfrac{r^{2}b^{2}}{a2}\right) + \left(termstobeneglected\right)\right\}$

$= \dfrac{1}{a}\left[n + \dfrac{n ( n + 1 )}{2} \cdot \dfrac{b}{a} + \dfrac{n ( n + 1 ) ( 2n + 1 )}{6} \cdot \dfrac{b2}{a2}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{a} \left[$n + \dfrac{n^{2} + n}{2} \cdot \dfrac{b}{a} + \dfrac{2n^{3} + 3n^{2} + n}{6} \cdot \dfrac{b2}{a2}\right]$

So \gamma = $\dfrac{b2}{3a^{3}}$

$

questions.q: Let& \left(a + bx + cx^{2}\right)10 = \mathop{∑}_{i = 10}^{20}{p}_{i}x^{i}, a, b, c \in \mathbb{N}$. If~${p}_{1} = 20$~and~${p}_{2} = 210$, then~$2  \left(a + b + c\right)$& is equal to& $
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that& \left(a + bx + cx^{2}\right)10 = \mathop{∑}_{i = 10}^{20}{p}_{i}x^{i}, a, b, c \in \mathbb{N}$

General term :~$\dfrac{10 !}{{r}_{1} ! {r}_{2} ! {r}_{3} !}\left(a\right){r}_{1}\left(bx\right){r}_{2}\left(cx^{2}\right){r}_{3}$

For coefficient. of~$x: {r}_{2} + 2{r}_{3} = 1$

Let~$\begin{cases}{r}_{1} & {r}_{2} & {r}_{3} \\ 9 & 1 & 0\end{cases}$

$∴$~coefficient of~$x = \dfrac{10 !}{9 !}a^{9}b^{1} = 20$

$⇒ a^{9} \cdot b = 2 . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Coefficient~of~$⇒ x^{2}: $\dfrac{10 !}{8 ! 2 ! 0 !}$a^{8} \cdotb^{2} + $\dfrac{10 !}{9 ! 0 ! 1 !} \cdota^{9} \cdotc =$210$

$⇒ 45a^{8} \cdotb^{2} + 10 \cdota^{9} \cdotc = 210$

$⇒ 9a^{8}b^{2} + 2a^{9} \cdotc = 42 . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

As~$a, b, c \in N$, so by hit and trial in equation~ \left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$~we get,~$a = 1, b = 2, c = 3$

Hence,~$2\left(a + b + c\right) = 2\left(3 + 2 + 1\right) = 12

$

questions.q: The lowest integer which is greater than ${\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{10}^{100}}\right)}^{{10}^{100}}$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Consider $P = {\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{10}^{100}}\right)}^{{10}^{100}},$

Let $x = {10}^{100}$

$⇒ P = {\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)}^{x}$

$⇒ P = 1 + \left(x\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + \dfrac{\left(x\right)\left(x - 1\right)}{⌊ 2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}} + \dfrac{\left(x\right)\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)}{\dfrac{3}{3}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{{x}^{3}} + \ldots$

(upto ${10}^{100} + 1$ terms)

$⇒ P = 1 + 1 + \left(\dfrac{1}{⌊ 2} - \dfrac{1}{\left⌊2x\right}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{⌊ 3} - \ldots\right) + \ldots$ so on

$⇒ P = 2 +$(Positive value less than $\dfrac{1}{⌊ 2} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 3} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 4} + \ldots$ )

Also $e = 1 + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 1} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 2} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 3} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 4} + \ldots$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{⌊ 2} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 3} + \dfrac{1}{⌊ 4} + \ldots = e - 2$

$⇒ P = 2 +$ (Positive value less than $e - 2$)

$⇒ P \in \left(2, 3\right)$

$⇒$ Least integer value of $P$ is $3 .$

questions.q: The remainder when \left(2021\right)2023$~is divided by~$7$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The remainder when $2021$ divided by $7$ is $- 2$. Hence, the problem reduces to finding the remainder when~\left(- 2\right)2023$~is divided by $7$.

$= \dfrac{\left(- 2\right)2022 \times \left(- 2\right)}{7}$

$= - \dfrac{2 \times {2}^{2022}}{7}$

$= \dfrac{- 2 \times \left({2}^{3}\right)674}{7}$

$= \dfrac{- 2 \times \left(8\right)674}{7}$

$= \dfrac{- 2 \times \left(1 + 7\right)674}{7}$

Using binomial theorem, we get

$= \dfrac{- 2 \times \left(1 + 7k\right)}{7}$~where~$k$~is an integer.

$= \dfrac{- 2 - 14k}{7}$

Clearly, the~remainder when~$- 14k$~is divisible by~$7$~is~$0$.

$= \dfrac{- 2}{7}$

$= \dfrac{- 2 - 5 + 5}{7} = \dfrac{5}{7}$

Hence, the remainder~is $5$.

$

questions.q: If the constant term in the expansion of \left(3x^{3} - 2x^{2} + \dfrac{5}{x5}\right)10$~is ${2}^{k} . l$, where $l$~is an odd integer, then the value of $k$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
For \left(3x^{3} - 2x^{2} + \dfrac{5}{x5}\right)10$the general term is given by

${T}_{r + 1} = \dfrac{10 !}{{r}_{1} ! {r}_{2} ! {r}_{3} !}\left(3\right){r}_{1}\left(- 2\right){r}_{2}\left(5\right){r}_{3}\left(x\right)3{r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} - 5{r}_{3}$

For term independent of~$x$~the exponent~$3{r}_{1} + 2{r}_{2} - 5{r}_{3} = 0 \ldots \left(1\right)$

Also we know~${r}_{1} + {r}_{2} + {r}_{3} = 10 ⋯ \left(2\right)$

From \left(1\right)$~and~ \left($2\right)$, we get~

${r}_{1} + $2\left($10 - {r}_{3}\right) - 5{r}_{3} = 0$

i.e.~${r}_{1} + 20 = 7{r}_{3}$

So~${r}_{1}, {r}_{2}, {r}_{3} = 1, 6, 3$

Hence the constant term~$= $\dfrac{10 !}{1 ! 6 ! 3 !}\left($3\$right)1\left(-$2\right)6\left(5\right)3$

$= {2}^{9} \cdot {3}^{2} \cdot {5}^{4} \cdot {7}^{1}$

$⇒ k = 9$

$

questions.q: If $Pr n = Pr + 1 n$ and~$Cr n = Cr - 1 n ,$~then the value of~$r$& is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& $Pr n = Pr + 1 n$

$⇒ \dfrac{n !}{\left(n - r\right) !} = \dfrac{n !}{ \left(n - r - 1\right) !}$

$⇒ \left(n - r\right) = 1 \ldots \left(1\right)$

and~$Cr n = Cr - 1 n$

$⇒ $\dfrac{n !}{r ! \left(n - r\right) !} = \dfrac{n !}{\left(r - 1\right) ! \left(n - r + 1\right) !}

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{r\left(n - r\right) !} = \dfrac{1}{ \left(n - r + 1\right)\left(n - r\right) !}$

$⇒ n - r + 1 = r$

$⇒ n + 1 = 2r \ldots \left(2\right)$

From equation~\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right),$~we get

$2r - 1 - r = 1$

$⇒ r = 2 .$

$

So,~$x - x^{'} = $2 \left[C1 13 \cdot \l$left(8\sqrt{3}\right)$12 \left($13\right)1 + C3 13 \l$left(8\sqrt{3}\right)$10 $\cdot \left(13\right)3 \ldots\right]$

Therefore, $x - x^{'}$ is~an even integer, hence \left[$x\right]$ is even

Now, $y = $\lleft(7\sqrt{2} +9\right)9 = C0 9 $\$lleft(7\sqrt{2}\right)$9 + C1 9 $\$lleft(7\sqrt{2}\rright)$8\left($9\right)1 + C2 9 $\lleft(7\sqrt{2}\rright)7\left($9\right)2 + . . . .$Now let,$y^{'} = ( $7\sqrt{2} -$9{)}^{9} = C0 9 ( $7\sqrt{2}{)}^{9} -$C1 9 ( $7\sqrt{2}{)}^{8} ($9{)}^{1} + C2 9 \$lleft(7\sqrt{2}\rright)7 \left($9\right)2$

So,~$y - y^{'} = $2 \left[$C1 9 \lleft(7\sqrt{2}\right)8 \left($9\right)1 + C3 9 $\$left(7\sqrt{2}\right)$6 \left(9\right)3 + \ldots\right]$

$y - y^{'} =$ Even integer hence \left[y\right]$ is even

$\begin{aligned} & (1+x)^{n+4} \\ & { }^{n+4} C_4,{ }^{n+4} C_5,{ }^{n+4} C_6, \rightarrow \text { A.P. } \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \times { }^{n+4} C_5={ }^{n+4} C_4+{ }^{n+4} C_6 \\ & \Rightarrow 4 \times{ }^{n+4} C_5=\left({ }^{n+4} C_4+{ }^{n+4} C_5\right)+\left({ }^{n+4} C_5+{ }^{n+4} C_6\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 4 \times{ }^{n+4} C_5={ }^{n+5} C_5+{ }^{n+5} C_6\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 4 \times \frac{(\mathrm{n}+4)!}{5!\cdot(\mathrm{n}-1)!}=\frac{(\mathrm{n}+6)!}{6!\cdot \mathrm{n}!} \\ & \Rightarrow 4=\frac{(\mathrm{n}+6)(\mathrm{n}+5)}{6 \mathrm{n}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}^2+11 \mathrm{n}+30=24 \mathrm{n} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}^2-13 \mathrm{n}+30=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=3,10(\text { rejected }) \\ & \because \mathrm{n} \neq 10\end{aligned}\therefore$ Largest binomial coefficient in expansion of
$\begin{aligned}
& (1+\mathrm{x})^7 \\
& (\because \mathrm{n}+4=7)
\end{aligned}$
is coeff. of middle term
$\Rightarrow{ }^7 \mathrm{C}_4={ }^7 \mathrm{C}_3=35$

questions.q: If $Pn - 1 2n + 1 : Pn 2n - 1 = 11: 21$, then ${n}^{2} + n + 15$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{Pn - 1 2n + 1}{Pn 2n - 1} = \dfrac{11}{21}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{\left(2n + 1\right) !}{\left(n + 2\right) !}}{\dfrac{\left(2n - 1\right) !}{\left(n - 1\right) !}} = \dfrac{11}{21}$

$⇒ 21 \times \dfrac{\left(2n + 1\right)2n\left(2n - 1\right) !}{\left(n + 2\right)\left(n + 1\right)n\left(n - 1\right) !} = 11 \times \dfrac{\left(2n - 1\right) !}{\left(n - 1\right) !}$

$⇒ 21 \times 2\left(2n + 1\right) = 11\left(n + 2\right)\left(n + 1\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(2n + 1\right)}{\left(n + 2\right)\left(n + 1\right)} = \dfrac{11}{42}$

Now on comparing both side we get, $n = 5$

So, the value of ${n}^{2} + n + 15 = {5}^{2} + 5 + 15 = 45$
